blockers.title: policyProvenance is simultaneously declared a string and an object, leaving the pre-existing-policy branch unsatisfiable
evidence: The policyProvenance member still declares type: string and nullable: true.

The same member now requires every present value to satisfy whenPresent.type: object with exactly authority, artifactPath, selector, and digest; requiredWhen makes such a present value mandatory for pre-existing-policy.

FC-CARRIER-SHAPE's only accepted pre-existing-policy row uses an object. That row satisfies whenPresent but violates the member's outer string type. Conversely, any string satisfying the outer type violates whenPresent. No JSON value can satisfy both constraints.

This contradiction is introduced by the HAE10-CX-01 repair: v10 asked for a typed source-identity object, but v11 added only the nested object constraint and did not update the member's existing outer type.
blockers.impact: The closed serialized scope has no lawful representation for the only carrier available in CI. A conforming validator must reject every pre-existing-policy record; one that accepts the fixture's object must ignore the member's declared type. That is a totality failure in the repaired authorization-to-doctor contract, not a cosmetic schema issue.
blockers.requiredRepair: Change policyProvenance's outer type to object (nullable true), or an equivalent explicit object-or-null union, so it agrees with whenPresent. Align the authorization-record source and doctorV4FieldMapping text if needed, and retain a fixture asserting that the concrete source-identity object passes both the outer and nested constraints while strings and malformed objects fail.
